analysis: All three changed files are test-only, so no production code, trust boundary or deployed control changes in the supplied evidence. ClusterServiceRestartingStopTests.swift replaces an inline ClusterService fixture with macs.startedLeaderService(...) (patch hunk at old 32-44, new 32). The helper's body is not in the supplied evidence. It is a test helper, so the risk is limited to weaker test fixtures. The file's remaining tests (lines 423-675) use a loopback-only counting coordinator at 127.0.0.1 on an ephemeral port. They cover cluster re-plan, stop and hand-over races under the command lock, and only assert behavior. LoopExitThinkingContinuationTests.swift and GenerationLoopExitThinkingServingTests.swift add tests for a loop-guard continuation. That production feature (LoopExitThinkingContinuation.splice, GenerationLoopExitThinking, EngineV2Bridge changes) is outside this batch's source. The tests show these behaviors: usage tokens are summed across the first row and the continuation; the continuation prompt is the original prompt plus all produced tokens plus the close marker; the continuation budget is bounded by the remaining output budget and an answer cap; there is no continuation when the budget is exhausted or the thought closed itself; a client cancel propagates to the continuation; and the continuation fails closed to a length finish. Relevant threat areas are T-010, cancellation propagation, and A-018 availability. The tests assert cancel propagation. Billing and usage accounting (completion tokens including the extra marker token) is asserted only in the test fixtures. The production implementation is not supplied, so integration should confirm that the production splice enforces the same budget and cancel semantics. The continuation re-prefills the prompt plus the thought. That is a resource consideration, and the tests show it is gated by the 256-token minimum budget. The prefix-cache and tenant-scoping interaction (T-041, cacheSalt on the continuation request) is not exercised in these tests. A production reviewer should check that the continuation request carries the same cacheSalt and encryption context. No findings are raised.
